title: Posture Assessment Failure Trends
exclusions: Does not replace enterprise SIEM correlation for unrelated threat classes. Does not constitute legal, regulatory, or executive attestation for 'Posture Assessment Failure Trends'. Does not cover entities explicitly scoped out in operational_exceptions.csv. Pair with sibling UCs in the same subcategory when the SPL surface alone cannot prove control effectiveness (see prerequisiteUseCases on UC-17.1.11).
evidence: Saved search uc_17_1_11_posture_assessment_failure_trends, dashboard panel tied to this UC, weekly CSV export archived to index=evidence with change-ticket reference, and git-tracked lookup baselines referenced in the search.

controlTest.positiveScenario: On a lab host or staging index, ingest sample events that satisfy all SPL filters for 'Posture Assessment Failure Trends'. Run the saved search manually and confirm at least one result row with populated severity or metric fields. Verify the alert action fires within one schedule interval and the output matches the dashboard table projection for UC-17.1.11.

dataSources: ISE posture assessment logs (`cisco:ise:posture`) Collected via Splunk Add-on for Cisco Security (Splunkbase 1352) modular input or scripted poll into the index named in the SPL.
app: Splunk_TA_cisco-ise — Splunk Add-on for Cisco Security (Splunkbase 1352)
spl:
index=nac sourcetype="cisco:ise:posture" earliest=-30d
| where posture_status="NonCompliant"
| timechart span=1d count by failure_reason
description: Time-series view of posture failures by policy and reason — distinguishes one-off issues from worsening fleet hygiene or a bad policy rollout.
value: Security operations teams correlate posture failures with external events like patch deployments and AV updates, measure remediation effectiveness, and identify specific posture checks that consistently fail across the endpoint fleet.
implementation: Normalize `failure_reason` from ISE. Alert when daily failures exceed 7-day baseline by >50%. Segment by AD group or location if extracted.
visualization: Line chart (failures over time by reason), Stacked area (failures by policy), Single value (failures vs prior week).
knownFalsePositives:
1. **Scheduled maintenance windows** — Planned change activity in the CMDB or change calendar produces expected deviations that match this detection pattern during approved maintenance. Cross-check ServiceNow change records for `state=implement` and the affected CI list.

2. **Backup and batch job cycles** — Nightly ETL, backup agents, or log rotation jobs generate bursts of similar events that resemble alert conditions but occur on a fixed schedule. Compare `_time` against the documented batch window before paging.

3. **Onboarding and provisioning bursts** — New users, devices, or services provisioned in bulk can temporarily skew counts until baselines stabilize. Filter events tagged `onboarding=true` in the identity or asset lookup.

4. **Monitoring and health-check traffic** — Synthetic transactions or internal scanner accounts generate probe traffic designed to exercise the control. Exclude service accounts listed in `monitoring_exceptions.csv`.

**Suppression mechanism:** Maintain a KV Store lookup `operational_exceptions.csv` with columns `entity`, `exception_reason`, `valid_from`, `valid_until`, and `approved_by`. Join the saved search to this lookup and filter `where isnull(exception_reason) OR now() > valid_until` so approved windows suppress alerts without muting the search globally.
detailedImplementation:
Prerequisites
• Cisco ISE Posture Module with AnyConnect ISE Posture Agent or Temporal Agent. Data in `index=nac` with `sourcetype=cisco:ise:syslog`. Key fields: `PostureStatus`, `PostureAssessmentFailure` (specific check that failed), `PostureRemediation` (action taken), `OperatingSystem`, `UserName`, `CallingStationID`.
• ISE Posture checks include: antivirus (installed, running, definitions updated), anti-malware, Windows patches, disk encryption (BitLocker/FileVault), firewall status, registry keys, application presence.
• Each posture requirement has a remediation action (install update, enable feature) and a grace period.

Step 1 — Configure data collection
Verify posture failure data:
```spl
index=nac sourcetype="cisco:ise:syslog" PostureStatus=NonCompliant earliest=-7d
| stats count by PostureAssessmentFailure, OperatingSystem
| sort - count
```

Step 2 — Create the search and alert

Primary search — Failure trend by check type:
```spl
index=nac sourcetype="cisco:ise:syslog" PostureStatus=NonCompliant earliest=-30d
| timechart span=1d count by PostureAssessmentFailure limit=10
```

Understanding this SPL: Trends posture failures over 30 days. Spikes correlate with external events: AV definition updates that fail to deploy, Windows Patch Tuesday (second Tuesday of the month), or ISE posture policy changes that introduce new requirements. A sustained increase in a specific failure type means the remediation is not working — the posture agent cannot fix the issue automatically.

Remediation effectiveness:
```spl
index=nac sourcetype="cisco:ise:syslog" earliest=-7d
| where PostureStatus="NonCompliant" OR PostureStatus="Compliant"
| sort CallingStationID _time
| streamstats current=f last(PostureStatus) as prev_status by CallingStationID
| where prev_status="NonCompliant" AND PostureStatus="Compliant"
| eval remediation_time_sec=_time - relative_time(_time, "-1h")
| stats avg(remediation_time_sec) as avg_remediation_sec dc(CallingStationID) as devices_remediated
```

Step 3 — Validate
(a) In ISE: Context Visibility > Endpoints > Compliance tab.
(b) Disable AV on a test device, reconnect, verify NonCompliant status appears.

Step 4 — Operationalize
Dashboard: Row 1 — Compliance rate trend. Row 2 — Failure types over time. Row 3 — Remediation effectiveness.
Alert: When any single posture check failure exceeds 50 affected devices in 24h.

Runbook:
1. **AV definition spike** — AV update server issue. Check WSUS/SCCM distribution point.
2. **Post-Patch-Tuesday spike** — Expected. Should resolve within 48h. If not, SCCM deployment stalled.
3. **New check introduced** — ISE posture policy change. Monitor the first 72h for impact.

Step 5 — Troubleshooting
• **PostureAssessmentFailure field empty** — ISE may not log specific check names. Enable detailed posture reporting in ISE.
• **NonCompliant count always high** — Posture policy may be too strict. Audit each posture requirement for necessity.

Step 1 — Configure data collection

Install and configure the add-on referenced in the app field (Splunk_TA_cisco-ise — Splunk Add-on for Cisco Security (Splunkbase 1352)). Enable the modular input or HEC token that writes sourcetype=cisco:ise:posture into nac. Default poll interval 300–900 seconds unless the vendor API rate-limits lower. Grant the ingestion role `list_inputs` and `search` on the target index.

Step 2 — Create the search and alert

Schedule the SPL with earliest=-24h@h and throttle per entity to avoid duplicate pages. Document tunable macros in the comment header. Understanding this SPL: filters in the first pipeline reduce license cost; stats/timechart aggregates define the alert grain; joins/lookups enrich owner or asset metadata for routing.

Step 3 — Validate

Compare `| tstats count where index=... sourcetype=...` against the vendor admin UI inventory count (+/-5%). Spot-check two known entities for field presence (`failure_reason`). Run `timechart count span=1h` over 7 days to find ingestion gaps longer than two poll intervals.

Step 4 — Operationalize

Add a dashboard row with single-value KPI tiles, a 24-hour timechart, and a drilldown table mirroring the SPL output columns. Route critical severity to the platform on-call channel; route warning to the service owner from the lookup.

Step 5 — Troubleshooting

No events: verify forwarder connectivity, HEC token ACLs, and that the modular input appears in `index=_internal source=*splunkd*`. NULL fields: check props/transforms order and TA version. Fewer results than expected: confirm index allow-lists on the search head role and that `_time` uses the correct timezone. API errors: inspect splunkd.log for HTTP 401/429 from the vendor endpoint configured in inputs.conf.
grandmaExplanation: We track which security checks devices fail when they connect — like having antivirus out of date or missing patches — and watch for patterns. If many devices suddenly fail the same check, it usually means an update did not deploy correctly, and we can fix it before it becomes a bigger problem.
